newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dollar see-saws,bond firm on RBA report.
newsitem.headline: Australian dollar see-saws,bond firm on RBA report.

text.p: The Australian dollar seesawed in an immediate reaction to the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) quarterly economic report, while debt futures firmed.
By 3.11 p.m. (0511 GMT) the dollar was US$0.7381/86 after dipping to US$0.7373/78 on the report in the central bank's August bulletin compared with US$0.7883/88 before its release.
The 10-year bond futures contract was 93.425 against a pre-report 93.395, while bill futures also firmed with the December contract moving to 95.26 from 95.23.
The RBA said present policy settings have scope to accomodate higher growth.
The central bank also said that domestic sourced inflation appears to be in check and that wage pressures have eased in recent months.
The RBA added that while growth is more likely to accelerate than slow down, second quarter demand and output expansion is likely to be at a slower pace than the first quarter.
